output.summary: A coniferous tree native to eastern Canada and the north-central and northeastern United States, northern white-cedar has fan-like branches, flat sprays of scale-like leaves and peeling red-brown bark. Some cliff-growing specimens are exceptionally old but remain small and stunted.
output.edibilityNote: Ojibwa reportedly made soup from soft-twig inner bark; twigs were also brewed as tea. Prolonged internal use or use during pregnancy may be harmful.
